title: How to reset your API key
text: CloudBox AI users can reset their API key from Account Settings > API Keys. After resetting the key, users must update the key in their application. Old keys stop working immediately after reset.

title: Fixing authentication error 401
text: A 401 authentication error usually means the API key is invalid, expired, missing, or used in the wrong environment. First confirm the copied key is correct and active. If the error continues after key reset, contact human support for account-level verification.

title: API key permissions and scopes
text: CloudBox AI API keys can have different scopes depending on the account plan and workspace role. A key without document search permission may fail for search requests even if the key is valid.

title: Billing overview
text: Billing for CloudBox AI subscriptions is managed from Settings > Billing. The billing page shows current plan, renewal date, payment method, and recent charges.

title: Refund policy
text: CloudBox AI offers refunds within 14 days of the initial subscription purchase for eligible self-serve plans. Refund requests made after 14 days are usually not approved automatically and may require human review.

title: How to cancel a subscription
text: Users can cancel their subscription from Settings > Billing > Manage Plan. Cancellation stops future renewals, but service remains active until the current billing period ends.

title: Inviting team members
text: Workspace admins can invite teammates from Team Settings > Members > Invite. Invitations are sent by email, and pending invitations remain visible until accepted or revoked.

title: Data privacy and storage
text: CloudBox AI stores uploaded files to provide document search and workspace access features. Customer data is processed according to the privacy policy. Requests involving legal review or special privacy guarantees should be handled by human support.

title: Resetting your password
text: Users can reset their password from the sign-in page by selecting Forgot Password. A reset email is sent to the registered email address. If no email arrives, users should check spam folders first.

title: Account deletion policy
text: Account deletion requests should be submitted to human support so the team can verify account ownership and explain data removal consequences. Workspace data access may be affected for all collaborators after deletion.

title: Document upload limits
text: CloudBox AI supports uploads up to 25 MB per file on the standard plan. Team and enterprise plans may allow larger files. Very large uploads can fail if the workspace storage quota is full.

title: How AI document search works
text: The search feature indexes uploaded documents and returns passages relevant to the query terms. Search quality improves when documents are clearly formatted and queries include specific keywords.

title: Supported file types
text: CloudBox AI supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, and Markdown file uploads. ZIP archives, executable files, and some image-only formats are not supported for document search indexing.

title: Troubleshooting failed uploads
text: If a document upload fails, check file size, supported format, network stability, and workspace storage availability. If the file type is unsupported, convert it to PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown before retrying.

title: Upgrading your plan
text: Users can upgrade from the billing page. Plan upgrades typically apply immediately, and prorated charges may appear on the next invoice depending on billing cycle timing.

title: Accessing invoices
text: Invoices and billing receipts are available in Settings > Billing > Invoices. Only billing admins can download invoice PDFs for team workspaces.

title: When human support is recommended
text: Human support is recommended for payment disputes, account deletion, legal or privacy concerns, repeated authentication failures after troubleshooting, and refund exceptions outside the standard policy.

title: Team roles and permissions
text: Only workspace admins can manage billing, invite members, revoke invitations, and change some API access settings. Regular members may not see admin-only controls in the interface.
